svg.title: Figure 9-3. Threat scenes: the risk-3 and risk-4 threat scenarios (WP-C-09 §9)
svg.desc: One card per threat scenario, the risk-3 and risk-4 threat scenarios: TS-05 Firmware signing below target lets other firmware pass as ours; TS-06 A malicious update reaches every device through the updater; TS-08 A build with SSH switched on gives root on the SoC; TS-01 Forged frames on the vehicle bus reach actuation and plausibility; TS-09 A tampered model file runs code when it is loaded; TS-07 Server-directed remote calls take data or open remote access; TS-10 A compromised upstream flows into every build; TS-12 Flooding the SoC starves the processes that drive; TS-13 Data signed with a stolen key passes as the device's own.
svg.text: Figure 9-3. Threat scenes: the risk-3 and risk-4 threat scenarios

Each card: where the threat sits in the risk matrix; what the damage looks like (schematic, loops every 6 s); how it gets there at the §5 level, with the missing control in red; what the item trusts; the feasibility factors and impact ratings.
Ratings, paths, risk and treatment from WP-C-09, goals from WP-C-10, in the order of the §9 top-risk table. No exploitation detail: the cards stay at the abstraction of §5.

g.title: TS-05: Firmware signing below target lets other firmware pass as ours
g.text: WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: Ability to build and flash panda firmware
Firmware with no assured envelope runs

g.text: “A firmware image that passes the signature
Firmware signing and the exclusion of debug capability are
below what CSG-02 needs. An image that passes the check need
not come from LionDriver. Details: GD-01, GD-02.
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-05) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility Medium; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)

g.title: TS-06: A malicious update reaches every device through the updater
g.text: WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Devices install it at the next update
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: Device installs it at the next update
Any SoC-rooted damage, on every device

g.text: “What the update source delivers is a
Updates are not authenticated end to end, so whoever controls
the update source controls every device that updates.
Automatic updates stay off until signed updates exist.
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-06) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility Medium; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)

SSH access and the SoC software
Root on the SoC: every SoC path

g.text: “Only the owner can log in to the device.”
Some builds can come with SSH already enabled and a key
installed. Anyone with that key and network reach gets root on
the SoC, and from there every SoC-rooted path. Release builds

g.title: TS-01: Forged frames on the vehicle bus reach actuation and plausibility
g.text: Forged frames on the vehicle bus reach
WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
A device on the OBD port or bus
Forged frames accepted as the car's own
The car brakes for nothing; follower closes
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: Physical access to the OBD-II port or bus
Forged frames injected on the car bus

g.text: “A frame with a valid checksum came from the
Received plausibility frames are not authenticated end to end,
so a device on the bus can forge them. Physical access is
needed, which keeps feasibility at Medium.
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-01) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility Medium; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)

g.title: TS-09: A tampered model file runs code when it is loaded
g.text: A tampered model file runs code when
WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
The driving model's output is theirs
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: A way to place a model file
no integrity check; load runs code
Code runs in the driving-model process

g.text: Model files are loaded in a format that can execute code, and
no hash or signature is checked at load. Whoever can place a
model file runs code in the driving-model process.
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-09) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility Medium; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)
